titulo: Change the channel, not the language
subtitulo: Mi può — plus whatever you need done. One frame, four repairs, and the smile-and-nod that costs you the afternoon
cena: The answer came back fast and friendly and you caught one word of it, and the queue behind you is not getting shorter.
frasePiso: When listening fails, change the channel before you change the language. Slower, written, or on the map — pick one and ask for that.

clique.desconto: Nobody gave you four different sentences for four different breakdowns. You kept one frame — mi può — and changed only the thing you needed done.
clique.piso: Next time an answer goes past you, you will not nod and hope. You will pick the repair you need and ask for that one.

steps.pt: The dangerous move is the polite nod at an answer you did not catch. It buys one second and costs you the afternoon.

steps.es: Allora, deve andare fino al semaforo e poi girare subito dopo il ponte.
steps.pt: So, you go up to the traffic light and then turn just after the bridge.
steps.tts: Allora, deve andare fino al semaforo e poi girare subito dopo il ponte.

steps.pt: Here is the frame: mi può, then the thing you need done. One opening, and you swap only the action.

steps.promptPt: Ask for the whole thing again, slower. Not louder — slower. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you repeat that more slowly?

steps.es: Certo. Fino al semaforo, poi a destra.
steps.pt: Of course. Up to the traffic light, then right.
steps.tts: Certo. Fino al semaforo, poi a destra.

steps.pt: Slower still fails when the payload is a number, a name or an address. Stop spending listening attempts on it.

steps.promptPt: Same frame, new action: ask them to write it down. Speak now.
steps.es: Me lo può scrivere, per favore?
steps.pinyin: meh lo pwoh SKREE-veh-re per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Can you write it down for me, please?
steps.tts: Me lo può scrivere, per favore?

steps.pt: Third channel: the map. A written street name can still leave three turnings unclear — hand over the phone.

steps.promptPt: Open the map and ask them to show you the point. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you show me on the map?

steps.es: Sì, guardi: è qui, dopo la piazza.
steps.pt: Yes, look: it's here, after the square.
steps.tts: Sì, guardi: è qui, dopo la piazza.

steps.pt: Fourth: cut the answer down before it grows. Asking if it is far turns a paragraph into a decision.

steps.promptPt: You only need to know whether to walk. Ask if it is far. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is it far?
No, five minutes on foot.
And the honest sentence that starts the whole ladder — say it plainly, with no apology attached.

steps.promptPt: You lost the thread. Say so, without apologising for existing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Sorry, I didn't understand.

steps.promptPt: Set the pace for the whole conversation, not just one sentence. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you speak more slowly?

steps.promptPt: Only the number was lost, not the whole answer. Ask for just that. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you repeat the number?

steps.promptPt: They were patient with you. Say so. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you, very kind.

steps.es: Scusi, non ho capito. Mi può ripetere più lentamente? Me lo può scrivere, per favore?
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee non oh ka-PEE-to. mee pwoh ree-PEH-teh-re pyoo len-ta-MEN-te. meh lo pwoh SKREE-veh-re per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Shadow the first three rungs, with no apology stacked on top.
steps.tts: Scusi, non ho capito. Mi può ripetere più lentamente? Me lo può scrivere, per favore?

steps.pt: B03 done. Mi può plus the action: slower, written, on the map. È lontano? shrinks the answer. The frame stays, the action changes.

aprofundar.titulo: Repair is a change of channel

secoes.corpo: Start with the smallest repair that could work. If slower succeeds, stop there. Move to writing only for payloads that stay fragile: numbers, names, addresses, times and medicine.

exemplos.pt: moves it out of your ears entirely

secoes.corpo: Asking someone to repeat usually gets you the same sentence louder, which does not help. Naming the change you want — slower — is what makes the second attempt different from the first.
A third identical attempt rarely changes the result. Writing externalises the detail and gives both people the same object to check, which is why it is the rung that ends most of these exchanges.

secoes.titulo: Non ho capito is not a confession
secoes.corpo: It is a status report, and it is normal. Every person in that queue has said it at some point. Delivered plainly, without a stacked apology, it reads as clarity rather than as weakness.

permissao: You are allowed to say non ho capito and mean it plainly, with nothing apologetic attached. Losing an answer in a noisy place is a normal part of a real conversation — the ladder exists precisely so you never have to fake understanding to keep things moving.
espelho: A tourist speaking English abroad does the exact same polite nod at a fast reply, and it produces exactly the same mess — the wrong platform, the wrong price, the wrong turn. It is not a weakness in your Italian; it is what anyone does under the small social pressure of not wanting to seem slow.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You nod and say grazie at an answer you did not actually catch, and ten minutes later you are on the wrong side of the river.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I did not want to hold up the queue, or make my Italian look worse than it is.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The nod protects the conversation for one more second and then hands you a real problem later, at a moment when the person who had the answer is gone and cannot help you fix it.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say non ho capito immediately — in the same breath as the nod you were about to give — and then pick a rung: slower, written, or on the map.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The correction happens while the person holding the answer is still in front of you, which is the only moment it is free.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not as a substitute for trying at all — saying non ho capito to every sentence without attempting the exchange reads as giving up rather than as repair.
